chukyu.word.2161.note.zh: 本课用法：平静下来；安定下来。 心が落ち着く：心情平静下来。

chukyu.word.2167.note.zh: 配合歌曲等做手部动作的游戏。

chukyu.word.2169.note.zh: 楽器を演奏する：演奏乐器。

chukyu.word.2172.note.zh: 効果的な方法：有效的方法。

chukyu.word.2179.note.zh: 効果をもたらす：带来效果。

word.2190.meaning.en: secret (method, trick, etc.); key (e.g. to success)

chukyu.word.2251.note.en: 日を浴びる: bask in the sun.

word.2263.meaning.en: to hum (a tune); to sing to oneself

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.meaning.zh: 片假名词；用口语询问词义
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.meaning.en: katakana word; asking for words in spoken terms

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.connection.zh: Nって何ですか。→ Nのことです。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.connection.en: Nって何ですか。→ Nのことです。

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.note.zh: 这里的「って」相当于提示话题的「は」，用于口语。ストレス、リラックス、カラオケ、ロック・フェスティバル都是片假名词。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.note.en: "って" here is equivalent to "は" for the subject. ストレス, リラックス, カラオケ, ロック, フェスティバル are katakana words.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.0.zh: “コンサート”是什么意思？就是音乐会。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.0.en: What does “コンサート” mean? It means a concert.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 很多人说，压力积累时会听音乐，让心情放松。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.1.en: A lot of people say that when stress accumulates, they listen to music and relax.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.3.zh: 暑假打算去摇滚音乐节。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.0.example.3.en: Summer's going to rock music festival.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词／い形容词普通形＋だろう；な形容词词干／名词＋だろう（不加だ）
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.connection.en: Verb/i-adjective plain form + だろう; na-adjective stem/noun + だろう (without だ).

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.note.zh: 「でしょう」的普通体，用于推测或委婉表达看法。不是表示过去的形式。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.note.en: The plain counterpart of でしょう, used for conjecture or a tentative opinion. It does not mark the past.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 音乐疗法最简单的方法，大概就是“听”吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.0.en: The simplest way to do music therapy is probably to listen.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 学习外语最好的方法，大概是去那个国家吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.1.en: The best way to learn foreign languages is to go to that country.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.2.zh: 这次音乐会有著名歌手参加，观众一定会很多吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.1.example.2.en: There'll be famous singers in this music. Must be a lot of audience.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 究竟……呢；提出疑问或自问
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.meaning.en: What the hell is it? Asking questions or asking yourself questions?

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.connection.zh: 普通形＋のだろうか；な形容词／名词的「だ」改为「な」
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.connection.en: Plain form + のだろうか; replace だ with な for nouns and na-adjectives.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.note.zh: 「のでしょうか」的普通体，常见于书面语，用来委婉提出疑问，也可表示思考、自问。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.note.en: The plain counterpart of のでしょうか, often used in writing for a tentative question, reflection or self-questioning.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 音乐疗法究竟听什么音乐才好呢？
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.0.en: What kind of music is music therapy?

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.1.zh: 敬语的用法很难。怎样才能记住呢？
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.1.en: It's hard to use words. How can I remember them?

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.2.zh: 为了放松，做什么才有效呢？
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.2.example.2.en: To relax, what does it do?

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词／い形容词普通形＋わけがない；な形容词＋な＋わけがない；名词＋の＋わけがない
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.connection.en: Verb/i-adjective plain form + わけがない; na-adjective + な + わけがない; noun + の + わけがない.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.note.zh: 根据常识或已知情况，强烈否定某种可能。句中若已有否定形式，整体可能表达强烈肯定。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.note.en: There is a strong rejection of a possibility based on common sense or known circumstances. If there is a negative form in the sentence, it may be a strong affirmation overall.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 听不喜欢的音乐，不可能放松。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.0.en: You can't relax when you don't like the music.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.1.zh: 他这么喜欢足球，不可能不看这场比赛。（一定会看）
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.1.en: He likes football so much, he can't stop watching the game.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.2.zh: 她工作总是很忙，不可能有空。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.3.example.2.en: She's always busy at work. She can't be free.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.connection.zh: わけがない：强烈否定可能性；わけではない：否定某个推论或概括
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.connection.en: わけがない: vehemently negative possibility; わけではない: negation of an inference or general

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.note.zh: 「わけではない」表示“并不是……”，不一定全盘否定；「毎日するわけではない」是“并非每天都做”。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.note.en: わけではない rejects an inference or generalization without necessarily denying everything. 毎日するわけではない means that the action is not done every day.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 不可能每天都在这么贵的餐厅吃饭。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.example.0.en: It's not possible to eat in such a expensive restaurant every day.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.4.example.1.zh: 会做饭，但并不是每天都做。

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 修饰名词时，主语的が有时可换成の
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.meaning.en: が of the main language can sometimes be replaced with の when noun is modified

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.connection.zh: 自分が好きな音楽 → 自分の好きな音楽
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.connection.en: 自分が好きな音楽 → 自分の好きな音楽

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.note.zh: 替换发生在修饰名词的从句内部，不适用于所有「が」。例如独立句「私が行きます」不能直接改成「私の行きます」。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.note.en: The replacement applies inside a noun-modifying clause, not to every が. The independent sentence 私が行きます cannot simply become 私の行きます.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.example.0.zh: 听自己喜欢的音乐，才真正能抚慰心灵。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.example.0.en: Listening to the music you like is the only way to really comfort your heart.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 来介绍一下我居住的城镇吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.5.example.1.en: Let's introduce the town I live in.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋ことこそ；名词＋こそ
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.connection.en: Verb dictionary form + ことこそ; noun + こそ.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.note.zh: 突出说话人认为最重要、最值得强调的部分。「今度こそ」常表达“这次一定要”的决心。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.note.en: Highlights what the speaker considers most important. 今度こそ often expresses determination to succeed this time.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.example.0.zh: 听自己喜欢的音乐，才真正能抚慰心灵。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.example.0.en: Listening to the music you like is the only way to really comfort your heart.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.example.1.zh: 每天写汉字，才是记住汉字的秘诀。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.example.1.en: Writing kanji every day is the secret to remember kanji.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.6.example.2.en: This exam has to be hard.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.meaning.zh: 并列内容中的重复动词可省略
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.meaning.en: Duplicate in parallel content verb may be omitted

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.connection.zh: 前后动作相同时，前半句可省去重复的动词
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.connection.en: The first half saves the verb from repeating when the action is the same.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.note.zh: 括号内是教材展示的省略部分。省略后仍需保证意思清楚，不能机械删除所有重复动词。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.note.en: The brackets are omitted from the presentation of the educational material. It is still necessary to make sure that the meaning is clear and that all duplicate verbs cannot be deleted mechanically.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.0.zh: 喜欢古典音乐的人听古典音乐，喜欢演歌的人听演歌，这是有效的方法。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.0.en: People who like classical music listen to classical music, people who like to play music listen to music, that's a good way to do it.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.1.zh: 能喝酒的人点了酒，不能喝的人点了果汁。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.1.en: The man who can drink ordered the wine, the man who can't drink the juice.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.2.zh: 平时步行上学，下雨时坐公交车上学。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.7.example.2.en: School is usually on foot and in a bus when it rains.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.connection.zh: より＋形容词／副词等，如「より難しく」「より多く」
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.connection.en: より + adjective/adverb, as in より難しく and より多く.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.note.zh: 本课的「より」单独作副词，表示程度进一步提高。注意与「AよりB」中表示比较基准的「より」区分。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.note.en: Here より is an adverb meaning a greater degree. Distinguish it from the comparison marker より in AよりB.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.0.zh: 音乐和声音能带来怎样的效果，今后将会受到更多关注吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.0.en: What music and sound can do will receive more attention in the future.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.1.zh: 日语学习进入中级后，会变得更难。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.1.en: Japanese language learning becomes more difficult when it enters the middle level.

chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.2.zh: 希望让更多人了解回收利用活动。
chukyu.lesson.1.grammar.8.example.2.en: It is hoped that recycling activities will be made more widely known.

chukyu.lesson.1.exerciseInstructions.zh: 先作答，再展开核对。第1—4题：いやされる、合わせる、演奏する、もたらす、たまる。第5—8题：さまざまな、したがって、最も、あまり、次第に。
chukyu.lesson.1.exerciseInstructions.en: Answer first, then expand to check. Questions 1–4: いやされる、合わせる、演奏する、もたらす、たまる. Questions 5–8: さまざまな、したがって、最も、あまり、次第に.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.0.note.zh: 带来怎样的效果：効果をもたらす。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.0.note.en: Use 効果をもたらす to describe producing an effect.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.1.note.zh: 「たまる」的て形是「たまって」，与いる连用。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.1.note.en: The て form of "たまる" is "たまって" associated with いる.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.2.note.zh: 「歌に合わせる」表示配合歌曲。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.2.note.en: 「歌に合わせる」means to follow the song.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.3.note.zh: 这里用被动形式，表示得到抚慰。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.3.note.en: Here's the passive form for comfort.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.5.note.zh: な形容词修饰名词「方法」。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.5.note.en: Use a na-adjective to modify the noun 方法.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.6.note.en: This is an indication of the changes that have occurred over time.

chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.7.note.zh: 根据上一句引出结论：“因此”。
chukyu.lesson.1.exercise.7.note.en: In the light of the preceding sentence, it is concluded that “so”.

chukyu.question.l1-g1.prompt.instruction.zh: 朋友问。最符合本课口语问答形式的回答是？
chukyu.question.l1-g1.prompt.instruction.en: Your friend asks the question above. Which answer matches this lesson’s conversational pattern?

chukyu.question.l1-g1.explanation.zh: 「Nって何ですか」询问名称或词义，可用「～のことです」解释。
chukyu.question.l1-g1.explanation.en: Nって何ですか asks about a name or word's meaning. Explain it with ～のことです.

chukyu.question.l1-g2.prompt.instruction.zh: 表示推测“明天大概很安静吧”
chukyu.question.l1-g2.prompt.instruction.en: Express a prediction: “It will probably be quiet tomorrow.”

chukyu.question.l1-g2.explanation.zh: な形容词在「だろう」前用词干：静かだろう。
chukyu.question.l1-g2.explanation.en: Use the na-adjective stem before だろう: 静かだろう.

chukyu.question.l1-g3.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达自问“为什么会这么不安呢”
chukyu.question.l1-g3.prompt.instruction.en: Wonder to yourself: “Why am I so anxious?”

chukyu.question.l1-g3.explanation.zh: な形容词接解释性的「のだろうか」时要加な：不安なのだろうか。
chukyu.question.l1-g3.explanation.en: Add な before the explanatory のだろうか with a na-adjective: 不安なのだろうか.

chukyu.question.l1-g4.prompt.instruction.zh: 强烈表达“不可能独自开车”
chukyu.question.l1-g4.prompt.instruction.en: Strongly express that driving alone is impossible.

chukyu.question.l1-g4.explanation.zh: 根据“才5岁”强烈否定能独自开车的可能，用「わけがない」。
chukyu.question.l1-g4.explanation.en: Being only five is strong evidence that he cannot drive alone. Use わけがない.

chukyu.question.l1-g5.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“我会喝咖啡，但并非每天都喝”，哪句最合适？
chukyu.question.l1-g5.prompt.instruction.en: Which sentence means “I drink coffee, but not every day”?

chukyu.question.l1-g5.explanation.zh: 「わけではない」否定“每天都喝”这个概括，不否定喝咖啡这件事。「わけがない」则强烈否定可能。
chukyu.question.l1-g5.explanation.en: "わけではない" rejects the general notion of "drink every day" and does not deny coffee. "わけがない" strongly rejects the possibility.

chukyu.question.l1-g6.prompt.instruction.zh: 把改成意思相同的名词修饰形式。
chukyu.question.l1-g6.prompt.instruction.en: Rewrite the quoted phrase as a noun-modifying expression with the same meaning.

chukyu.question.l1-g6.explanation.zh: 修饰名词「町」的从句中，主语的が可换成の：私の住んでいる町。
chukyu.question.l1-g6.explanation.en: In the clause modifying 町, the subject marker が can become の: 私の住んでいる町.

chukyu.question.l1-g7.prompt.instruction.zh: 强调“每天坚持练习才是关键”
chukyu.question.l1-g7.prompt.instruction.en: Emphasize that practicing every day is the key.

chukyu.question.l1-g7.explanation.zh: 辞书形＋ことこそ强调“正是坚持这件事”。さえ表示“连……都”，まで表示范围扩展，しか需与否定呼应。
chukyu.question.l1-g7.explanation.en: Dictionaryform + ことこそ It was stressed that “it is precisely this thing that persists”. さえ It says, "Even..." まで It's an extension of the scope. しか It needs to be echoed in the negative.

chukyu.question.l1-g8.prompt.instruction.zh: 省去括号中的重复动词后，仍能保留原意的是哪句？
chukyu.question.l1-g8.prompt.instruction.en: Which sentence retains its meaning after the repeated verb in brackets is omitted?

chukyu.question.l1-g8.explanation.zh: 前后都是“喝”，可以省去前面的飲み。其余选项前后动作不同，省略会改变原意。
chukyu.question.l1-g8.explanation.en: Both actions are drinking, so the first 飲み can be omitted. The other options describe different actions; omission would change the meaning.

chukyu.question.l1-g9.prompt.instruction.en: Express the wish for more people to take part.

chukyu.question.l1-g9.explanation.zh: 题目要求表达相较现在“更多”的人，用より多く。かなり是相当多，少し是少量，最も是最多，均不等于“更多”。
chukyu.question.l1-g9.explanation.en: Use より多く for more people than now. かなり means considerably, 少し means a little, and 最も means the most; none means more in this comparison.

chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.0.zh: 说话人确信他绝不会忘记约定。
chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.0.en: The speaker is certain that he will never forget the promise.

chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.1.zh: 说话人确信他会忘记约定。
chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.1.en: The speaker is certain that he will forget the promise.

chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.2.zh: 说话人认为他不一定会忘记约定。
chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.2.en: The speaker thinks he will not necessarily forget the promise.

chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.3.zh: 说话人认为他有可能忘记约定，但并不确定。
chukyu.question.l1-g10.option.3.en: The speaker thinks he may forget the promise, but is not certain.

chukyu.question.l1-g10.explanation.zh: 「忘れないわけがない」否定“不忘记”的可能，即认为一定会忘记。注意双重否定。
chukyu.question.l1-g10.explanation.en: 忘れないわけがない denies the possibility of not forgetting, so the speaker expects to forget. Pay attention to the double negative.

chukyu.word.2279.note.zh: 本课用法：汉语圈；汉语使用地区。
chukyu.word.2279.note.en: Use of the course: Chinese Circle; Chinese-speaking area.

chukyu.word.2282.note.zh: 本课用法：讨厌；厌恶。 嫌われる：被讨厌。
chukyu.word.2282.note.en: In this lesson: to dislike; to hate. 嫌われる: to be disliked.

word.2285.meaning.en: to be obsessive (about); to be overly concerned (with)

chukyu.word.2285.note.zh: 本课用法：讲究；执着于。 数字にこだわる：讲究数字。
chukyu.word.2285.note.en: In this lesson: to be particular about; to be fixated on. 数字にこだわる: to be particular about numbers.

chukyu.word.2286.note.zh: 本课用法：号码；编号。 本课语境中指车牌号码。
chukyu.word.2286.note.en: This course is used: No.; No. In the context of this course, it refers to the number of the licence plate.

chukyu.word.2288.note.en: The present course is used for: the rich; the rich.

chukyu.word.2289.note.zh: 本课用法：因此；为此。 本课表示原因、结果之间的联系。
chukyu.word.2289.note.en: This course is used: therefore; for this purpose, it indicates the connection between the cause and the result.

chukyu.word.2291.note.zh: 本课用法：几……；数……。 数千万円（すうせんまんえん）：数千万日元。
chukyu.word.2291.note.en: In this lesson: several; a number of. 数千万円（すうせんまんえん）: tens of millions of yen.

chukyu.word.2292.note.zh: 本课用法：标上；定下。 値段がつく：定出价格；拍出价格。
chukyu.word.2292.note.en: In this lesson: to be assigned or set. 値段がつく means to acquire a price or fetch a price at auction.

chukyu.word.2293.note.en: This course is used for the drawing of lots and drawing of lots.

chukyu.word.2294.note.zh: 本课用法：中签；抽中。 抽選に当たる：抽签中选。
chukyu.word.2294.note.en: In this lesson: to win a drawing. 抽選に当たる: to be selected in a lottery.

word.2296.meaning.zh: 放入（「手に入れる」表示得到）
word.2296.meaning.en: put in; let in (手に入れる means obtain)

chukyu.word.2296.note.zh: 本课用法：放入；取得。 手に入れる：得到；弄到手。
chukyu.word.2296.note.en: In this lesson: to obtain. 手に入れる: to get; to acquire.

chukyu.word.2297.note.zh: 本课用法：牌；牌照。 本课指车牌。
chukyu.word.2297.note.en: This course is used: license plate; license plate.

word.2304.meaning.en: to long for; to yearn for

word.2309.meaning.en: joining a company; getting a job with a company

word.2311.meaning.en: change of job; change of occupation

word.2330.meaning.zh: 合不合得来；相处是否融洽

word.2332.meaning.en: to tell someone's fortune; to divine (the future)

word.2334.meaning.en: basis for decision; evidence for judging

word.2336.meaning.en: fortunetelling based on writing or pronunciation of one's name

word.2340.meaning.en: to make (the best) use of; to put to good use

word.2348.meaning.en: to be divisible (by); to be divided without residue (remainder)

word.2350.meaning.en: have something in common; be connected

word.2355.meaning.en: one class (of students); one group (of people)

word.2360.meaning.en: half the amount (of money); half price

chukyu.word.2363.note.zh: 幸運が訪れる：幸运降临。
chukyu.word.2363.note.en: 幸運が訪れる: good fortune arrives.

word.2364.meaning.en: to like; to be pleased with

word.2365.meaning.en: conclusion (of an argument, discussion, study, etc.)

word.2368.meaning.en: spring, summer, autumn (fall) and winter; the four seasons

chukyu.word.2373.note.zh: 本课用法：进入。 目に入る：进入眼中；映入眼帘。
chukyu.word.2373.note.en: In this lesson: to enter. 目に入る: to come into view; to catch one's eye.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.meaning.zh: 称为……的；说明名词的内容
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.meaning.en: called ...; description of the content of noun

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.connection.zh: 普通形＋という＋名词；名词1＋という＋名词2
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.connection.en: plain form + という + noun; noun 1+ という + noun 2

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.note.zh: 表示名称、具体内容或定义。口语常用「っていう」或「って」。名词／な形容词谓语表达内容时保留「だ」，如「冬は暖冬だという予想」。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.note.en: Introduces a name, content or definition. In conversation, という often becomes っていう or って. Keep だ in noun/na-adjective predicates expressing content, as in 冬は暖冬だという予想.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 在越南，“4”这个数字被认为是好数字之一。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.0.en: In Viet Nam, the “4” figure is considered to be one of the good figures.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 有很多意见认为不能赞成这个计划。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.1.en: There were many views that the plan could not be endorsed.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.2.zh: 昨天发布了今年冬天将是暖冬的预测。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.2.en: Yesterday, a forecast was released that this winter will be warm.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.3.zh: A：你认识一个叫山田的人吗？ B：不认识，是谁？
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.0.example.3.en: A: Do you know a man called Yamada? B: No. Who is it?

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋ことほど＋……はない；名词＋ほど＋……はない／いない
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.connection.en: verb commentary form + ことほど ＋…… はない ;noun+ ほど ＋…… はない ／ いない

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.note.zh: 以某事物为最高程度的比较基准。「いない」用于人、动物等有生命的存在；「ない」用于事物或情况。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.note.en: The highest level of comparison is based on something. " いない" is used for the existence of humans, animals, etc.; "ない " is used for things or situations.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 没有哪个地方比汉语圈更讲究“好数字”。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.example.0.en: There is no place where "good numbers" are more pronounced than in the Chinese language.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 没有比读书更快乐的事。

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.example.2.zh: 没有人像佐藤那样认真学习。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.1.example.2.en: No one learns as hard as Sato.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.meaning.en: To the extent that: ... to the extent ...

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.connection.zh: 动词辞书形／ない形＋ほど；动词辞书形／ない形＋ぐらい・くらい
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.connection.en: verb dictionary form/ ない Form+ ほど ;verbdictionaryform/ ない Form+ ぐらい ・ くらい

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.note.zh: 通过具体例子或比喻说明程度。「ぐらい／くらい」常用于口语。本课将「死ぬほど」这类极端比喻与一般程度表达区分，练习中用「死ぬほど疲れた」。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.note.en: Uses an example or comparison to express degree. ぐらい／くらい are common in conversation. This lesson distinguishes extreme comparisons such as 死ぬほど from ordinary degree expressions and practices 死ぬほど疲れた.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 拍出了数千万日元以上、令人吃惊的价格。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.0.en: The price of tens of millions of yen or more has been filmed as amazing.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.1.en: I'm so tired of moving my friends.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.2.zh: 大地震晃得让人站都站不住。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.2.en: The big earthquake is shaking people to the ground.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.3.zh: 拍出了数千万日元以上、令人吃惊的价格。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.3.en: The price of tens of millions of yen or more has been filmed as amazing.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.4.zh: 昨天走了一整天，今天早上脚痛得几乎站不起来。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.2.example.4.en: Yesterday, all day, my feet were barely standing up this morning.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.note.zh: 既可表示站在某人的立场看问题，也可表示以某种线索为依据作判断。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.note.en: It can be expressed either to look at the issue in a person ' s position or to judge on the basis of certain leads.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 从日本人的角度看，这是难以想象的事。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.example.0.en: From the Japanese perspective, this is inconceivable.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.example.1.zh: 从那身穿着来看，他似乎不是公司职员。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.3.example.1.en: From that look, he does not seem to be an employee of the company.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.connection.zh: 含疑问词的小句＋か＋より、～
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.connection.en: Words with questionable words + か ＋ より 、～

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.note.zh: 把两个问题或关注点作比较。前项常有「どんな」「いくら」等疑问词，用「か」把疑问小句嵌入句中。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.note.en: Compares two questions or concerns. The first clause often contains a question word such as どんな or いくら and is embedded with か.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 比起拥有什么车，更重视挂着什么号码的车牌。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.example.0.en: More important than having a car, is the number plate.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.example.1.zh: 工作比起工资多少，内容更重要。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.4.example.1.en: Work is more important than wages.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 数字的读法：从0～10到十、百、千、万

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.connection.zh: 先记基本数字，再按位组合：十（じゅう）→百（ひゃく）→千（せん）→万（まん）。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.connection.en: Learn the basic numbers, then combine place values: 十（じゅう）→百（ひゃく）→千（せん）→万（まん）.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.note.zh: 本项为补充学习内容。0也读れい，4也读し，7也读しち，9也读く；本练习优先使用ゼロ・よん・なな・きゅう，便于清楚报数。数字与日期、时间、量词搭配时可能有不同读法，如四月（しがつ）、四時（よじ），不能机械套用。先看数字读一遍，再点击发音核对；也可遮住数字，只听读音后写下数字。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.note.en: Supplementary number practice. 0 also has the reading れい, 4 has し, 7 has しち, and 9 has く. This exercise uses ゼロ・よん・なな・きゅう for clarity. Dates, times and counters may require different readings, such as 四月（しがつ）and 四時（よじ）. Read each number, then check its pronunciation; alternatively, cover the number and write what you hear.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.0.zh: 两位数先读几十，再读个位：21读「にじゅういち」。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.0.en: Read the tens before the units: 21 is にじゅういち.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 按数量读数时，空缺的位不读零：105不是「ひゃくゼロご」。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.1.en: Skip empty place values when reading quantities: 105 is not ひゃくゼロご.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.2.zh: 从大到小依次读千、百、十、个位。100、1,000单独表示数量时通常读ひゃく、せん。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.2.en: Read thousands, hundreds, tens and units in order. Standalone quantities 100 and 1,000 are usually ひゃく and せん.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.3.zh: 万位开始以万分组：1万＋2千＋50。万前面的1要读いち。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.3.en: From 万 upward, group numbers in units of ten thousand: 1万＋2千＋50. Pronounce the 1 before 万 as いち.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.4.zh: 注意百位的音变；不是さんひゃく、ろくひゃく、はちひゃく。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.4.en: Watch the sound changes in hundreds; not さんひゃく, ろくひゃく or はちひゃく.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.5.zh: 注意千位的音变；不是さんせん、はちせん。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.5.en: Watch the sound changes in thousands; not さんせん or はちせん.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.6.zh: 逐位报编号时，每个数字单独读，开头的0也要读出来；不要读成数量123。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.6.en: When numbering by place, each numeral is read separately and the beginning zero is also read out; do not read to number 123.

chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.7.zh: 这本书800日元。金额中的800仍读はっぴゃく。
chukyu.lesson.2.grammar.5.example.7.en: This book costs 800 yen. The amount 800 is still read はっぴゃく.

chukyu.lesson.2.exerciseInstructions.zh: 先作答，再展开核对。第1—4题：こだわる、入れる、とる、つく、嫌う。第5—8题：抽選、縁起、手数料、仲間、偶数。
chukyu.lesson.2.exerciseInstructions.en: Answer first, then expand to check. Questions 1–4: こだわる、入れる、とる、つく、嫌う. Questions 5–8: 抽選、縁起、手数料、仲間、偶数.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.0.note.zh: 「値段がつく」表示定出价格；先週提示过去时间。「ついた」也可以。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.0.note.en: 値段がつく means to be assigned a price. 先週 indicates past time. ついた is also acceptable.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.1.note.zh: 「手に入れる」表示得到，接「ことができた」前用辞书形。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.1.note.en: 手に入れる means to obtain. Use its dictionary form before ことができた.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.2.note.en: Use the dictionary form to modify the noun 人.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.3.note.zh: 「例にとる」表示以……为例；连接后句用て形。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.3.note.en: 例にとる means to take something as an example. Use the te-form to connect to the next clause.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.4.note.zh: 偶数（ぐうすう）：能被2整除的整数。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.4.note.en: Even numbers (ぐうすう): integers divisible by two.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.5.note.zh: 「縁起のいい／悪い」表示吉利／不吉利。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.5.note.en: 縁起のいい／悪い means auspicious/inauspicious.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.6.note.zh: 手数料（てすうりょう）：手续费。这是教材练习句，实际收费依银行规定而定。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.6.note.en: 手数料（てすうりょう）means a service fee. This is a textbook exercise; actual fees depend on the bank.

chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.7.note.zh: 「抽選に当たる」表示抽签中选。
chukyu.lesson.2.exercise.7.note.en: 抽選に当たる means to win a lottery or drawing.

chukyu.question.l2-g1.prompt.instruction.zh: “名叫青空的咖啡馆”应说：青空（　　　）喫茶店。

chukyu.question.l2-g1.explanation.zh: 「名称＋という＋名词」介绍名称：青空という喫茶店。
chukyu.question.l2-g1.explanation.en: A name + という + noun introduces a name: 青空という喫茶店.

chukyu.question.l2-g2.prompt.instruction.zh: 选择自然的句子，表达“公布了明天停课的通知”。
chukyu.question.l2-g2.prompt.instruction.en: Choose the natural sentence meaning “A notice was issued that tomorrow’s classes are canceled.”

chukyu.question.l2-g2.explanation.zh: 内容小句中的名词谓语保留だ：明日は休校だ＋という知らせ。
chukyu.question.l2-g2.explanation.en: Keep だ in the noun predicate of the content clause: 明日は休校だ＋という知らせ.

chukyu.question.l2-g3.prompt.instruction.en: What is the natural conversational version of this sentence?

chukyu.question.l2-g3.explanation.zh: っていう是という的口语形式。「という人を知っていますか」仍是原来的敬体表达；「と一緒にいる人」表示和田中在一起的人；「に似ている人」表示像田中的人，意思不同。
chukyu.question.l2-g3.explanation.en: っていう is the conversational form of という. という人を知っていますか retains the original polite wording. と一緒にいる人 means a person with Tanaka; に似ている人 means a person resembling Tanaka. These have different meanings.

chukyu.question.l2-g4.prompt.instruction.zh: 哪一句表达“对我来说，没有比在海边散步更放松的事”？
chukyu.question.l2-g4.prompt.instruction.en: Which sentence means “For me, nothing is more relaxing than walking by the sea”?

chukyu.question.l2-g4.explanation.zh: ことほど～はない表示最高程度。「あまり～できない」表示不太能放松；「家で休むほうが」表示在家更放松；「少しは」表示能稍微放松，均不同于“最放松”。
chukyu.question.l2-g4.explanation.en: ことほど～はない expresses the highest degree. あまり～できない means not being able to relax much; 家で休むほうが means being more relaxed at home; 少しは means relaxing a little. None expresses the most relaxed.

chukyu.question.l2-g5.explanation.zh: 比较对象是有生命的「先生」，存在的否定用いない：没有像佐藤老师这样耐心教人的老师。
chukyu.question.l2-g5.explanation.en: 先生 refers to a living person, so use いない: there is no teacher who teaches as patiently as Sato.

chukyu.question.l2-g6.explanation.zh: 「Vない＋ほど」用具体情况说明程度：摇晃得站都站不住。
chukyu.question.l2-g6.explanation.en: Vない＋ほど expresses degree through a concrete situation: shaking so much that one cannot stand.

chukyu.question.l2-g7.prompt.instruction.zh: 帮朋友搬家后，用夸张的程度表达说“累得要命”，哪句最合适？
chukyu.question.l2-g7.prompt.instruction.en: After helping a friend move, use an exaggerated expression meaning “exhausted to death.”

chukyu.question.l2-g7.explanation.zh: 死ぬほど疲れた表示累得要命。「疲れたわけではない」否定疲劳；「疲れるはずがない」否定疲劳的可能；「疲れたのだろうか」自问是否疲劳，均没有肯定极强的疲劳程度。
chukyu.question.l2-g7.explanation.en: 死ぬほど疲れた means extremely tired. 疲れたわけではない denies being tired; 疲れるはずがない denies the possibility of fatigue; 疲れたのだろうか questions whether one is tired. None affirms extreme fatigue.

chukyu.question.l2-g8.prompt.instruction.zh: 从那位客人的口音判断，他似乎来自大阪
chukyu.question.l2-g8.prompt.instruction.en: Judge from the visitor’s accent that they seem to be from Osaka.

chukyu.question.l2-g8.explanation.zh: 从口音这一线索作判断用からすると。にとって表示立场与评价，に比べて表示比较，を中心に表示以……为中心。
chukyu.question.l2-g8.explanation.en: To judge from this line of accent, からすると. にとって expresses position and evaluation, に比べて compares, and を中心に is centered.

chukyu.question.l2-g9.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“买电脑时，比起价格多少，更重视是否好用”
chukyu.question.l2-g9.prompt.instruction.en: Express that ease of use matters more than price when buying a computer.

chukyu.question.l2-g9.explanation.zh: 「値段がいくらか」是含疑问词的嵌入小句。小句后接より，与后项关注点比较。
chukyu.question.l2-g9.explanation.en: 値段がいくらか is an embedded clause containing a question word. Follow it with より to compare the two concerns.

chukyu.question.l2-g10.prompt.instructio.en: Which meaning is closest to this sentence?

chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.0.zh: 和家人共度时光并不重要。
chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.0.en: Spending time with family is not important.

chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.1.zh: 和家人共度时光是最重要的事。
chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.1.en: Spending time with family is the most important thing.

chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.2.en: It is impossible to spend time with family.

chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.3.zh: 和家人相处的时间太短了。
chukyu.question.l2-g10.option.3.en: Too little time is spent with family.

chukyu.question.l2-g10.explanation.zh: 「～ほど～はない」通过“没有比……更……”表达最高程度。
chukyu.question.l2-g10.explanation.en: ～ほど～はない expresses the highest degree by saying that nothing is more … than the comparison item.

chukyu.question.l2-g11.prompt.instructio.zh: 表示数字0的常见读法是哪组？
chukyu.question.l2-g11.prompt.instructio.en: Which group gives common readings of the number 0?

chukyu.question.l2-g11.explanation.en: Regularly read ゼロ or れい.

chukyu.question.l2-g12.prompt.instructio.zh: 哪组正确对应4、7、9的清楚报数读法？
chukyu.question.l2-g12.prompt.instructio.en: Which group gives clear counting readings for 4, 7, and 9?

chukyu.question.l2-g12.explanation.zh: 本练习采用よん・なな・きゅう。4、7、9还有し・しち・く等读法，使用场景不同。
chukyu.question.l2-g12.explanation.en: This exercise uses よん・なな・きゅう. The numbers 4, 7 and 9 also have readings such as し・しち・く, depending on context.

chukyu.question.l2-g13.prompt.instructio.en: What is the correct reading of 300?

chukyu.question.l2-g13.explanation.zh: 300发生浊音变化，读さんびゃく；さんぜん是3,000。
chukyu.question.l2-g13.explanation.en: 300 has changed sound, reading さんびゃく; さんぜん is 3,000.

chukyu.question.l2-g14.explanation.zh: 600读ろっぴゃく，800读はっぴゃく，两者都有小っ和ぴゃく。
chukyu.question.l2-g14.explanation.en: 600 reads ろっぴゃく and 800 read はっぴゃく, both of which are small っ and ぴゃく.

chukyu.question.l2-g15.explanation.zh: 3,000读さんぜん，8,000读はっせん。さんびゃく、はっぴゃく是300、800。
chukyu.question.l2-g15.explanation.en: 3,000 read さんぜん and 8,000 read はっせん. さんびゃく, はっぴゃく are 300, 800.

chukyu.question.l2-g16.explanation.zh: 10,000是一万，读いちまん。せん是1,000，じゅうまん是100,000，ひゃくまん是1,000,000。
chukyu.question.l2-g16.explanation.en: 10,000 is 10,000, reading いちまん. せん is 1,000, じゅうまん is 100,000, ひゃくまん is 1,000,000.

chukyu.question.l2-g17.prompt.instructio.en: What is the correct reading of the quantity 12,050?

chukyu.question.l2-g17.explanation.zh: 12,050＝一万＋二千＋五十，读いちまんにせんごじゅう。空缺的百位、个位不读零。
chukyu.question.l2-g17.explanation.en: 12,050＝一万＋二千＋五十, read いちまんにせんごじゅう. Do not read zero for the empty hundreds and units places.

chukyu.question.l2-g18.prompt.instructio.zh: 逐位报练习编号「0123」，应该怎样读？
chukyu.question.l2-g18.prompt.instructio.en: Read the practice code “0123” digit by digit.

chukyu.question.l2-g18.explanation.zh: 逐位报编号时保留开头的0。ひゃくにじゅうさん表示数量123，不是逐位报号。
chukyu.question.l2-g18.explanation.en: Keep the beginning 0 at the place-by-place number. ひゃくにじゅうさん represents a volume of 123, not a place-to-place entry.

chukyu.word.100015.note.zh: 10年ほど：十年左右。本课词表中表示概数。

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词て形＋以来；表示时间或事件的名词＋以来
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.connection.en: Verb te-form + 以来; a noun referring to a time or event + 以来.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.note.zh: 以前面的事件为起点，表示状态持续或动作反复发生到现在或某个参照时间。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.note.en: Start with the preceding events, indicating that the state continues or is repeated to the present or at a given reference time.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 自从来到日本后，多次听到“面白い”这个词。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.0.en: Since coming to Japan, I have heard the word 面白い many times.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 自从进公司以来，我和他像朋友一样，无论什么事都会互相商量。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.1.en: Ever since he joined the company, I've been like a friend to talk to each other about everything.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.2.zh: 自从半年前和家人通电话后，就一直没有联系。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.0.example.2.en: No contact has been made since the telephone conversation with the family six months ago.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.connection.en: 何 + counter + も; 何 + counter + か.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.note.zh: 「何回も・何人も・何年も」强调次数、人数或时间之多。「何人か」表示不确定的若干人，通常不强调数量大。不要把「何～も」与「何も～ない」混同。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.note.en: 何回も, 何人も and 何年も emphasize a large number of times, people or years. 何人か means an unspecified few people, not necessarily many. Distinguish 何～も from 何も～ない (nothing / not anything).

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 已经多次听到“面白い”这个词。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.0.en: I have already heard the word 面白い many times.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 今天早上电车出了事故，好多人迟到了。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.1.en: There was an accident in the tram this morning, and a lot of people were late.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.2.en: I haven't seen him in years.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.3.zh: 考试结果不理想，有几名学生不及格。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.1.example.3.en: The results of the examinations were unsatisfactory and several students failed.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 指代前文内容；区分双方是否共有认知
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.meaning.en: Refers to the preceding text; distinguishing between the two sides whether or not they share a common understanding

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.connection.zh: 文章：これ／それ等；会话：それ／あの等
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.connection.en: In writing: これ／それ, etc. In conversation: それ／あの, etc.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.note.zh: 文章中的「こ・そ」可指前文内容；「こ」常将内容作为自己身边或自己关注的事来谈。会话中，在回指已知事物时，双方都知道的常用「あ」，只有一方知道、另一方刚听说的常用「そ」。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.note.en: The article 'こ . そ ' may refer to the previous text; 'こ' often refers to it as a matter of personal or personal concern. In sessions, when referring to what is known, both parties know the usual 'あ' and only one party knows, and the other has just heard, the usual 'そ '

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 别人常说“你真有意思”。这算是在夸我吗？
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.0.en: People say, "You're funny." Is that a compliment?

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.1.zh: 他的记忆力非常好，但从不以此自夸。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.1.en: His memory is very good, but he never boasts about it.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.2.zh: A：昨天我去了花山公园。 B：那个公园在哪里？
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.2.en: A: Yesterday I went to Hanayama Park. B: Where is that park?

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.3.zh: A：明天我要去看横滨的烟花大会。 B：啊，那个烟花大会非常有名吧。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.2.example.3.en: A: I'm going to the fireworks conference in Yokohama tomorrow. B: Ah, the fireworks conference is very famous.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.connection.zh: 普通形＋ということだ；口语可说「っていうことだ」
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.connection.en: Plain form + ということだ; conversational form: っていうことだ.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.note.zh: 本课用来根据事实引出结论或换一种说法解释。不应与表示传闻的「ということだ」混淆。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.note.en: This lesson is used to draw conclusions or a different interpretation based on facts. It should not be confused with the anecdotal "ということだ " .

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 也就是说，这个词是善意的，而不是否定性的。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.0.en: That is, the term is good faith and not negative.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.1.zh: A：这就是事实。 B：也就是说，那个说法是假的，对吧。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.1.en: A: That's the truth. B: In other words, it's a fake, right?

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.2.zh: A：C是素食者。 B：那就是说，肉和鱼都不吃吗？
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.3.example.2.en: A:C is a vegetarian. B: Does that mean that neither meat nor fish eat?

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋までもない；动词辞书形＋までもなく＋后句
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.connection.en: Verb dictionary form + までもない; verb dictionary form + までもなく + following clause.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.note.zh: 事情已经很明显，或不值得特意采取某个行动。「までもなく」用于连接后文；常见「言うまでもなく」（不言而喻）。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.note.en: It has become clear that something is not worth taking. " までもなく " is used to connect to the back; commonly " 言うまでもなく " (specify).

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 不言而喻，日本是认真的。（教材中的省略表达）
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.0.en: It goes without saying that Japan is serious.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.1.zh: 这是大家都知道的事，不必特意说明。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.1.en: This is a matter for all to know, and there is no point in saying it.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.2.zh: 不用举哆啦A梦为例，日本动画也已为很多人所熟知。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.4.example.2.en: The Japanese animation is well known to many people without the need to do A dream.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.meaning.en: Whether it is ...; whether it is ... or...

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.connection.zh: どこの国／どんな人／どんな時＋であろうと；名词1＋であろうと、名词2＋であろうと
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.connection.en: どこの国／どんな人／どんな時 + であろうと; noun 1 + であろうと、noun 2 + であろうと.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.note.zh: 书面表达，相当于「疑问词＋名词＋でも」。列举两项时表示两者均适用。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.note.en: Written expression, equivalent to "question word + noun + でも " . The listing indicates that both apply.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.0.zh: 无论哪个国家，我想都会有有趣的发现。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.0.en: I think there's something interesting going on in any country.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 无论什么人，都应该有良心。

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.2.zh: 无论什么时候，都希望不迷失自我。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.2.en: At any time, hope is not to lose yourself.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.3.zh: 有人遗弃宠物。但是，无论是人还是动物，都应该同样珍惜其生命。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.5.example.3.en: Some abandon their pets. But humans and animals alike should cherish their lives.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.meaning.zh: 移动后的状态；变化后的状态

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.connection.zh: 行く→行っている；来る→来ている；戻る→戻っている；帰る→帰っている
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.connection.en: 行く→行っている；来る→来ている；戻る→戻っている；帰る→帰っている

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.note.zh: 本课重点不是“正在移动”，而是已移动并处于结果状态。例如「会場に行っている」表示已经去了会场。也可表示恢复等变化的结果状态，如「元の状態に戻っている」。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.note.en: The focus is the resulting state after movement, rather than movement in progress. 会場に行っている means that someone has already gone to the venue. 元の状態に戻っている describes a restored state.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.0.zh: 我来自地球的另一侧。（已经来到这里）
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.0.en: I'm from the other side of the planet.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.1.zh: A：负责人已经去会场了吧。 B：是的，收到联系说正在会场检查资料。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.1.en: A: The person in charge has already gone to the conference room. B: Yes, they have been contacted and said they are checking the information at the meeting site.

chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.3.zh: 上周身体不舒服，不过现在已经恢复原状。
chukyu.lesson.3.grammar.6.example.3.en: Last week was not well, but it has now been restored.

chukyu.lesson.3.exerciseInstructions.zh: 先作答，再展开核对。第1—4题：配られる、満ちる、押しのける、変わる、暮らす。第5—7题：否定的な、失礼な、好意的な、酒臭い、思いがけない。最后一题有两个空。
chukyu.lesson.3.exerciseInstructions.en: Answer first, then expand to check. Questions 1–4: 配られる、満ちる、押しのける、変わる、暮らす. Questions 5–7: 否定的な、失礼な、好意的な、酒臭い、思いがけない. The last question has two blanks.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.0.note.zh: 「配られる」的て形：配られて。表示正在被免费分发。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.0.note.en: The te-form of 配られる is 配られて. It describes being distributed free of charge.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.1.note.zh: 「暮らす」去掉ます的词干接たい：暮らしたい。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.1.note.en: Attach たい to the masu-stem of 暮らす: 暮らしたい.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.2.note.en: 「愛情に満ちている」: full of love.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.3.note.zh: 连接后句用连用形「押しのけ」；「押しのけて」也可连接后句。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.3.note.en: Use the continuative form 押しのけ to connect to the following clause. 押しのけて also works.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.4.note.zh: 「失礼」为な形容词，修饰「態度」用失礼な。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.4.note.en: 失礼 is a na-adjective. Use 失礼な to modify 態度.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.5.note.zh: 意想不到的事情：思いがけない出来事。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.5.note.en: An unexpected event: 思いがけない出来事.

chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.6.note.zh: 两个空分别表示否定与善意；互换顺序也成立。两者修饰「意味」都要加な。
chukyu.lesson.3.exercise.6.note.en: The two blanks express a negative intention and goodwill; either order is acceptable. Both adjectives take な before 意味.

chukyu.question.l3-g1.explanation.zh: 动词接以来用て形：働き始めて以来，自从开始在日本工作以来。
chukyu.question.l3-g1.explanation.en: Use the te-form before 以来: 働き始めて以来, “since starting work in Japan.”

chukyu.question.l3-g2.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“自从毕业以来一直住在这里”
chukyu.question.l3-g2.prompt.instruction.en: Express “I have lived here ever since graduating.”

chukyu.question.l3-g2.explanation.zh: 事件名词可直接接以来：卒業以来。后句说明持续状态。
chukyu.question.l3-g2.explanation.en: The following sentence describes the status quo.

chukyu.question.l3-g3.prompt.instruction.zh: 强调“已经提醒好多次了”
chukyu.question.l3-g3.prompt.instruction.en: Emphasize that you have already given the warning many times.

chukyu.question.l3-g3.explanation.zh: 「何＋量词＋も」强调次数多。何回か仅表示不确定的几次。
chukyu.question.l3-g3.explanation.en: 何＋counter＋も emphasizes a large number of occurrences. 何回か means an unspecified few times.

chukyu.question.l3-g4.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“有几名学生缺席”，不强调人数很多
chukyu.question.l3-g4.prompt.instruction.en: Express “several students are absent,” without emphasizing a large number.

chukyu.question.l3-g4.explanation.zh: 「何人か」表示不确定的若干人；「何人も」强调人数之多。
chukyu.question.l3-g4.explanation.en: 何人か means an unspecified few people; 何人も emphasizes a large number of people.

chukyu.question.l3-g5.prompt.instruction.zh: B没听说过这家店，追问位置。B应说？
chukyu.question.l3-g5.prompt.instruction.en: B has not heard of this café and asks where it is. What should B say?

chukyu.question.l3-g5.explanation.zh: 只有A知道这家店，B回指刚听到的内容时用そ系列。其余选项暗示已有共同认知。
chukyu.question.l3-g5.explanation.en: Only A knows the store, and B refers to the そ series when you hear it. The rest of the options imply a common understanding.

chukyu.question.l3-g6.explanation.zh: 今天是店休日，因此可得出今天休息的结论：休みだということですね。其余选项不能直接接在题干已有的「休みだ」之后构成目标句型。
chukyu.question.l3-g6.explanation.en: Today is the shop's closing day, so the conclusion is 休みだということですね. The other options cannot follow the existing 休みだ to form the target pattern.

chukyu.question.l3-g7.prompt.instruction.zh: 大家都知道这件事，无须特意解释
chukyu.question.l3-g7.prompt.instruction.en: Everyone knows this, so there is no need to explain it.

chukyu.question.l3-g7.explanation.zh: までもない表示无须特意解释。わけがない表示不可能，ことになっている表示规定，にすぎない表示只不过，均不表达“没有必要”。
chukyu.question.l3-g7.explanation.en: までもない indicates that there is no need for a deliberate explanation. わけがない indicates that it is not possible, ことになっている states that にすぎない simply does not mean "necessary".

chukyu.question.l3-g8.prompt.instruction.en: Express “Needless to say, health is important.”

chukyu.question.l3-g8.explanation.zh: 言うまでもなく表示不言而喻。言うわけもなく偏向没有理由／不可能说，言うはずもなく是否定说的可能，言うこともなく表示没有说。
chukyu.question.l3-g8.explanation.en: 言うまでもなく means “needless to say.” 言うわけもなく suggests no reason or possibility of saying it; 言うはずもなく denies the likelihood of saying it; 言うこともなく means without saying it.

chukyu.question.l3-g9.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“无论什么工作，我都想认真去做”
chukyu.question.l3-g9.prompt.instruction.en: Express “Whatever the job is, I want to do it seriously.”

chukyu.question.l3-g9.explanation.zh: 「疑问词＋名词＋であろうと」表示无论哪一种，后项都适用。
chukyu.question.l3-g9.explanation.en: "Question word + noun + であろうと" means that the latter entry applies either way.

chukyu.question.l3-g10.prompt.instructio.zh: 这里「行っています」表示？
chukyu.question.l3-g10.prompt.instructio.en: What does 行っています express in this conversation?

chukyu.question.l3-g10.option.1.zh: 已经去了会场，现在处于到达后的状态。
chukyu.question.l3-g10.option.1.en: Has already gone to the venue and is now there.

chukyu.question.l3-g10.option.2.en: Has never been to the venue.

chukyu.question.l3-g10.option.3.en: Only plans to go to the venue next year.

chukyu.question.l3-g10.explanation.zh: 移动动词＋ている在这里表示移动后的结果状态。上下文明确他已在会场准备。
chukyu.question.l3-g10.explanation.en: Move verb + ている here indicates the result state after the move. The context makes clear that he is ready for the session.

chukyu.word.2512.note.en: Usage of the course: light; light.

chukyu.word.2515.note.zh: 本课用法：耀眼的；刺眼的。
chukyu.word.2515.note.en: This course is about the bright and the sharp.

word.2518.meaning.en: to crowd out; to push out

word.2522.meaning.en: to take in; to bring in

chukyu.word.2522.note.zh: 本课用法：收进；吸收；摄入。
chukyu.word.2522.note.en: This course uses: Intake; Absorption; Ingestion.

chukyu.word.2523.note.en: This course is used: brain; brain.

word.2524.meaning.en: to spread (of a rumour, news, etc.); to travel

chukyu.word.2524.note.en: This course is used to: pass on; pass on.

chukyu.word.2525.note.zh: 本课用法：引起；使发生。 くしゃみを起こす：引起喷嚏。他动词。
chukyu.word.2525.note.en: Cause; bring about. くしゃみを起こす: cause sneezing. Transitive verb.

chukyu.word.2528.note.en: This lesson is used: itchy; itchy souffle.

word.2531.meaning.en: inside and outside the country; domestic and foreign

chukyu.word.2531.note.en: Use of the course: National and international.

chukyu.word.2532.note.zh: 自覚症状がある：有自己能感受到的症状。
chukyu.word.2532.note.en: 自覚症状がある: have symptoms one can feel.

chukyu.word.2536.note.zh: 本课用法：一般的；普遍的。
chukyu.word.2536.note.en: Use of the course: General; Universal.

chukyu.word.2537.note.en: This course is used for parents and children.

word.2538.meaning.en: look exactly alike; be the spitting image of

chukyu.word.2538.note.zh: 本课用法：一模一样的；酷似的。 声がそっくりだ：声音一模一样。
chukyu.word.2538.note.en: In this lesson: identical; very similar. 声がそっくりだ: the voices sound exactly alike.

chukyu.word.2539.note.zh: 本课用法：很有意思的；引人深思的。

word.2549.meaning.en: to jump in; to leap in

word.2561.meaning.zh: 下班时间；结束工作时间

word.2566.meaning.en: student preparing for or taking examinations (usu. entrance exams); test-taker

word.2569.meaning.en: Do not rush onto the train.

word.2575.meaning.en: to be delighted; to be glad

word.2577.meaning.en: before one's very eyes; under one's nose

word.2607.meaning.en: to fall down; to fall over

word.2610.meaning.en: to be surprised; to be taken aback

word.2611.meaning.en: to be amazed; to be shocked

word.2614.meaning.en: to be blessed with; to be rich in

word.2615.meaning.en: address; call out to; place on

word.2622.meaning.en: to be packed (with); to be filled

chukyu.word.100025.note.zh: 男女差がある：存在男女差异。
chukyu.word.100025.note.en: 男女差がある: there are differences between men and women.

chukyu.word.100026.note.en: 実際の音: the actual sound.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.note.zh: 前项发生后，紧接着出现意料之外的变化。后项通常不接说话人的意志、请求或命令。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.note.en: The latter does not normally follow the will, request or order of the person who speaks.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 刚觉得刺眼，就“阿嚏”一声打出了喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.0.en: When I felt the eyes pierced, "Sneezing" sneezed.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 下课铃刚响，学生们就走出了教室。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.1.en: When the bell rang, the students walked out of the classroom.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.2.zh: 他一钻进被窝就睡着了。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.0.example.2.en: He fell asleep as soon as he got into the nest.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.connection.zh: 去掉ます后＋だす／込む：飛びだす、降りだす、吸い込む、走り込む
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.connection.en: Masu-stem + だす／込む: 飛びだす, 降りだす, 吸い込む, 走り込む.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.note.zh: 「だす」可表示向外出现，也可表示突然开始。「込む」可表示向内移动，也可表示深入、充分地做某事。不同复合动词的意思需结合词汇学习。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.note.en: だす can express outward movement or a sudden beginning. 込む can express inward movement or doing something deeply or thoroughly. Learn each compound verb in context.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 刚觉得刺眼，喷嚏就打了出来。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.0.en: I just felt a sting and sneezed out.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 刚上电车，他就从包里拿出了平板电脑。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.1.en: Just got on the tram, and he took the tablet out of the bag.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.4.zh: 因为太热，就跳进了游泳池。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.4.en: Because it's too hot to jump into the pool.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.5.zh: 马拉松选手为比赛每天练习，进行充分的跑步训练。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.1.example.5.en: Marathon players practiced daily for the competition and conducted adequate running training.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.meaning.en: With; at the same time; with ...

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.connection.zh: 名词＋とともに（一起）；动词辞书形＋とともに（同时）；动词辞书形／名词＋とともに（伴随变化）
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.connection.en: Noun+ とともに (joint); verb dictionary form+ とともに verb dictionary form / noun + とともに (According to change)

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.note.zh: 区分三个意思：共同做事、同时进行两件事、一方变化伴随另一方变化。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.note.en: Three meanings are distinguished: to do things together, to do two things simultaneously, and one change with the other.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 试图把进入鼻子的异物连同鼻涕一起排到外面。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.0.en: Trying to line the alien into the nose with the snot.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.1.zh: 与志愿者伙伴一起，让镇上的活动取得了成功。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.1.en: Working with volunteer partners to make town activities successful.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.2.zh: 发生了电车事故。公司一边调查事故原因，一边推进恢复运行的工作。

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.3.zh: 随着人口增加，垃圾问题也出现了。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.3.en: As the population grows, the problem of garbage also emerges.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.4.zh: 随着经济复苏，买房的人越来越多。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.2.example.4.en: As the economy recovers, more and more people buy houses.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 把助词短语变成修饰名词的形式
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.meaning.en: Turn the synonym into a modified form of noun

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.connection.zh: で／から／まで／と／へ＋の＋名词；表示对象或目的地的「に」常改为「への」
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.connection.en: で ／ から ／ まで ／ と ／ へ ＋ の +noun; for object or destination ' に It's always changed to " への 」

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.note.zh: 例如「学校で生活する→学校での生活」。本课不使用「がの」「をの」；不能机械地给所有助词加の。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.note.en: For example: 学校で生活する→学校での生活. This lesson does not use がの or をの; do not mechanically add の to every particle.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 来自眼睛的“刺眼”信号传到大脑。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.0.en: The signal of the eye is passed on to the brain.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.1.zh: 怀念与父母一起生活的日子。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.1.en: Remember the day you live with your parents.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.2.zh: 期待去泰国的毕业旅行。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.3.example.2.en: I'm looking forward to my graduation trip to Thailand.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋途中（で／に）；名词＋の＋途中

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.note.zh: 表示移动或某个过程尚未完成的阶段。「途中で」常用来说明在这个阶段发生了另一件事。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.note.en: Indicates the stage at which a move or a process has not been completed. " 途中で" is often used to describe another event that occurred at this stage.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 来自眼睛的信号传向大脑的过程中，不知为什么鼻子发痒，打出了喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.example.0.en: The signal from the eye was passed on to the brain, and for some reason the nose itches and sneezes.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.example.1.zh: 回家途中，在图书馆借了书。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.4.example.1.en: On his way home, he borrowed books at the library.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 模仿声音；描写感觉或状态
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.meaning.en: imitating sound; describing feelings or state

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.connection.zh: 拟声：はくしょん、ワンワン。拟态：むずむず等＋する；ぺこぺこ等＋だ
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.connection.en: Sound imitation: はくしょん, ワンワン. Manner/state words: むずむず + する; ぺこぺこ + だ.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.note.zh: 教材列出的身体感觉词：むずむず（痒酥酥）、どきどき（心怦怦跳）、にこにこ（微笑）、はらはら（提心吊胆）、むかむか（恶心／生气）、がんがん（头疼得厉害等）、ひりひり（火辣辣地疼）＋する；ぺこぺこ（肚子饿）、からから（干渴）、くたくた（疲惫不堪）＋だ。意思随语境变化。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.note.en: The manual lists the words of physical feeling: むずむず (Itchy sobs) どきどき (heart beats) にこにこ (Smiling) はらはら (EXHALES) むかむか (disgusting/grunting) がんがん (headache waiting) ひりひり (spiring) + する ； ぺこぺこ (I'm hungry.) からから (Dry) くたくた ♪ Tired ♪ だ . Meaning changes in context.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.0.zh: 刚觉得刺眼，就“阿嚏”一声打出了喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.0.en: When I felt the eyes pierced, "Sneezing" sneezed.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 邻居家的狗“汪汪”地叫，很吵。

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.2.zh: 鼻子痒痒的，打出了喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.2.en: The nose itches and sneezes out.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.3.zh: 从早上开始什么都没吃，肚子饿扁了。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.5.example.3.en: I haven't eaten anything since morning. I'm starving.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.connection.zh: 动词た形／い形容词／な形容词＋な＋ことに
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.connection.en: verb た shape/ い impact/ な impact+ な + ことに

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.note.zh: 先表达说话人的感受，再说明引起这种感受的事情。常见「驚いたことに」「面白いことに」「残念なことに」。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.note.en: Express the speaker's feeling first, then explain what caused it. Common forms include 驚いたことに、面白いことに、残念なことに.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.0.zh: 有趣的是，有一种说法是父母与子女打喷嚏的声音非常相似。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.0.en: Interestingly, there is a statement that the sound of parents sneezing with their children is very similar.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.1.zh: 令人困扰的是，不太清楚这个镇上垃圾的丢弃方法。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.1.en: It's disturbing that there's no clear way to dump the trash in this town.

chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.2.zh: 遗憾的是，运动会因台风取消了。
chukyu.lesson.4.grammar.6.example.2.en: Unfortunately, the Games were cancelled by typhoons.

chukyu.lesson.4.exerciseInstructions.zh: 先作答，再展开核对。第1—4题：飛びだす、押しだす、遺伝する、表す、吸い込む。第5—8题：そっくり、実際の、効果的な、一般的な、きっかけ。
chukyu.lesson.4.exerciseInstructions.en: For questions 1–4, choose from 飛びだす, 押しだす, 遺伝する, 表す and 吸い込む and change the form as needed. For questions 5–8, choose from そっくり, 実際の, 効果的な, 一般的な and きっかけ.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.0.note.zh: 「くしゃみが飛び出す」表示突然打出喷嚏；「飛びだす」写法也可。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.0.note.en: "くしゃみが飛び出す" means suddenly sneezing; "飛びだす" can also be written.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.1.note.zh: 「音を表す」表示表达声音。礼貌疑问句用表しますか；普通体「表すか」也成立。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.1.note.en: 音を表す means to express a sound. Use 表しますか for a polite question; the plain form 表すか also works.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.2.note.zh: 传闻「普通形＋そうだ」；这是教材中的语言练习句。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.2.note.en: Rumor has it " plain form + そうだ " ; this is a language practice from a textbook.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.3.note.zh: 用辞书形修饰名词「パワー」：吸入垃圾的吸力。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.3.note.en: Modifier noun "パワー": the sorbent of inhaling garbage.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.4.note.zh: 「声がそっくりだ」表示声音非常相似。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.4.note.en: 「声がそっくりだ」means the voices sound very alike.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.5.note.zh: 开始学习的契机：勉強を始めたきっかけ。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.5.note.en: 勉強を始めたきっかけ: the occasion that prompted someone to start studying.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.6.note.zh: な形容词接「ようだ」要用「一般的なようだ」。这是教材例句。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.6.note.en: A na-adjective before ようだ takes な: 一般的なようだ. This is a textbook example.

chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.7.note.zh: 名词「実際」修饰「音」时加の。
chukyu.lesson.4.exercise.7.note.en: Add の when the noun 実際 modifies 音.

chukyu.question.l4-g1.explanation.zh: 刚打开门，猫马上意外地冲出去，用「Vたとたん」。
chukyu.question.l4-g1.explanation.en: The cat unexpectedly rushes out immediately after the door opens. Use Vたとたん.

chukyu.question.l4-g2.prompt.instruction.zh: 表达“刚躺下就睡着了”，哪一句接续正确？
chukyu.question.l4-g2.prompt.instruction.en: Choose the correct connection meaning “I fell asleep as soon as I lay down.”

chukyu.question.l4-g2.explanation.zh: とたん前接动词た形：横になったとたん。
chukyu.question.l4-g2.explanation.en: とたん follows the verb's ta-form: 横になったとたん.

chukyu.question.l4-g3.prompt.instruction.en: What does だす express in this sentence?

chukyu.question.l4-g3.option.0.en: Take rain out of a bag.

chukyu.question.l4-g3.explanation.zh: 复合动词「降りだす」中的だす表示开始，常带突然发生的感觉。
chukyu.question.l4-g3.explanation.en: だす in the compound verb 降りだす marks the start of an action, often with a sense of suddenness.

chukyu.question.l4-g4.prompt.instruction.en: Choose the expression meaning “breathe in air.”

chukyu.question.l4-g4.explanation.zh: 吸い込む表示向内吸入。吸いだす是抽吸出来，吐きだす是吐出，吹きだす是吹出或喷出，方向和动作不同。
chukyu.question.l4-g4.explanation.en: 吸い込む indicates inhalation. 吸いだす is snorting out, 吐きだす is vomiting, 吹きだす is blowing out or ejecting, different direction and movement.

chukyu.question.l4-g5.prompt.instruction.en: Express “complete the work together with my companions.”

chukyu.question.l4-g5.explanation.zh: とともに表示与同伴一起。に代わって表示替代，にとって表示评价立场，を通じて表示经由，均不等于一起完成。
chukyu.question.l4-g5.explanation.en: とともに indicates that it is with its peers. に代わって indicates substitution, にとって indicates an evaluation position, and を通じて indicates that it was passed and not done together.

chukyu.question.l4-g6.prompt.instruction.en: What does とともに express in this sentence?

chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.0.en: Go out together with one's age.

chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.1.zh: 随着一方变化，另一方也发生变化。
chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.1.en: As one thing changes, another changes too.

chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.2.zh: 刚到某个年龄就突然发生一次意外。
chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.2.en: An accident suddenly happens upon reaching a certain age.

chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.3.zh: 没有比年龄更重要的事。
chukyu.question.l4-g6.option.3.en: Nothing is more important than age.

chukyu.question.l4-g6.explanation.zh: 前后都是逐渐变化，とともに表示伴随变化，相当于随着。
chukyu.question.l4-g6.explanation.en: The changes have been gradual, and the とともに indicates that they are associated with the changes and are equivalent to the changes.

chukyu.question.l4-g7.prompt.instruction.zh: 把「友達と旅行する」改为“与朋友的旅行”：友達（　　　）旅行。
chukyu.question.l4-g7.prompt.instruction.en: Change 友達と旅行する to the noun phrase meaning a trip with friends: 友達（　　　）旅行.

chukyu.question.l4-g7.explanation.zh: 原句用と标记共同旅行的伙伴，修饰旅行时变为との。への表示方向，からの表示来源，での表示地点或场合。
chukyu.question.l4-g7.explanation.en: The original sentence uses と to mark a partner travelling together and modifies it to との. への indicates the direction, からの indicates the source, での indicates the location or venue.

chukyu.question.l4-g8.explanation.zh: 「动词辞书形＋途中で」表示在某个过程或路途中发生另一件事。
chukyu.question.l4-g8.explanation.en: "verb description form + 途中で" means another thing that happens in a process or on the way.

chukyu.question.l4-g9.prompt.instruction.zh: 从早上起没吃东西，肚子饿扁了
chukyu.question.l4-g9.prompt.instruction.en: You have eaten nothing since morning and are very hungry.

chukyu.question.l4-g9.explanation.zh: ぺこぺこ形容肚子饿。にこにこ是微笑，はらはら是担心，ひりひり是火辣辣地疼。
chukyu.question.l4-g9.explanation.en: ぺこぺこ describes hunger. にこにこ is a smile, はらはら is a concern, ひりひり is a hot pain.

chukyu.question.l4-g10.explanation.zh: な形容词＋な＋ことに，先表达感受再说明事情：残念なことに。
chukyu.question.l4-g10.explanation.en: Na-adjective＋な＋ことに expresses a feeling before describing the situation: 残念なことに.

chukyu.word.2630.note.en: 9月の半ば: the middle of September.

word.2669.meaning.en: to finish; to make an end of

word.2709.meaning.en: to serve as; to act as

word.2717.meaning.en: performance (as opposed to practice); going before an audience or on-air

word.2719.meaning.en: full bloom (esp. of cherry blossom); full blossom

word.2729.meaning.en: foot (of a mountain or hill); bottom

word.2732.meaning.en: to touch; to come in contact with

chukyu.word.100028.note.zh: 造られる（つくられる）：被建造。
chukyu.word.100028.note.en: 造られる（つくられる）: be built.

chukyu.word.100029.note.zh: 本课指到来。幸運が訪れる（こううんがおとずれる）：幸运降临。
chukyu.word.100029.note.en: In this lesson: to arrive. 幸運が訪れる（こううんがおとずれる）: good fortune arrives.

chukyu.word.100030.note.zh: 包まれる（つつまれる）：被包围。穏やかな空気に包まれる：笼罩在宁静的气氛中。
chukyu.word.100030.note.en: 包まれる（つつまれる）: to be surrounded. 穏やかな空気に包まれる: to be enveloped in a peaceful atmosphere.

chukyu.word.100032.note.en: The building, street etc. presents a pattern or atmosphere.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.meaning.zh: 正在逐渐……；变化正在进行

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词ます形去掉ます＋つつある
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.connection.en: verb ます takes off ます+ つつある

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.note.zh: 书面语，表示动作或作用向某一方向逐渐变化。常与変化する、変わる、増加する、増える、減少する、減る、なる等搭配。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.note.en: Written expression for gradual change in a direction. Often used with 変化する、変わる、増加する、増える、減少する、減る、なる.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 三井公园也正逐渐显露秋天的气息。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.0.en: Sani Park is also emerging as the autumn season unfolds.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 事故的原因正在逐渐明朗。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.1.en: The causes of the accident are becoming clear.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.2.zh: 人们对工作的价值观正在发生变化。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.0.example.2.en: The value of people working is changing.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.note.zh: 以某个地点、事物或人群为中心或主要对象。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.note.en: A particular location, thing or group of persons is central or the main target.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 公园围绕一大一小两个池塘建造。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.0.en: The park is built around a large, small two ponds.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 日本以东京为中心发展经济。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.1.en: Japan has an economy centred on Tokyo.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.2.zh: 日本酒正受到以年轻女性为主的人群的关注。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.1.example.2.en: The Japanese wine is receiving attention from a predominantly young female population.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 在做完某个移动动作后的地点
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.meaning.en: At a location after you've finished some movement.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.connection.zh: 动词た形＋ところに／ところで
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.connection.en: verb た + ところに / ところで

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.note.zh: 本课表示地点。「に」标示存在地点，「で」标示动作发生地点。不要与表示时间的「たところ」混淆。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.note.en: This course shows the location. " に " indicates where it exists, and " で " indicates where the action is taking place. Do not confuse with "たところ " which represents the time.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 沿池边小路走一小段，就有长椅。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.0.en: There are benches for a small walk along the edge of the pool.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.1.zh: 直走过去的地方有洗手间。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.1.en: There's a bathroom where you go straight over.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.2.zh: 请在过了下一个信号灯的地方停车。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.2.example.2.en: Please stop at the next light.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 意志动词与非意志动词的整理
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.meaning.en: Collation of Will Verb with Non-Will Verb

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.connection.zh: 意志动词：行く、作る、相談する等；非意志动词：ある、分かる、できる、行ける、見える、降る、吹く等。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.connection.en: Volitional verbs: 行く、作る、相談する. Non-volitional verbs: ある、分かる、できる、行ける、見える、降る、吹く.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.note.zh: 意志动词表示能够由本人决定做不做的行为。非意志动词表示存在、自然现象、能力或自然感知等，不能只凭本人意志控制；可能形式如「行ける」属于后者。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.note.en: Will verb indicates that it is possible to do the act in its own right. Non-consensual verb means existence, natural phenomena, ability or perception of nature, etc., cannot be controlled solely by its own will; the Potential form form, like " 行ける " , belongs to the latter.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 休息日的早晨，我经常去公园。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.0.en: In the morning of the rest day, I often go to the park.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.1.zh: 将来想创办自己的公司。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.1.en: I want to start my own company.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.2.zh: 打算明天向前辈请教工作方面的事。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.2.en: It is intended to teach the past about work tomorrow.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.3.zh: 沿小路走一小段的地方有长椅。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.3.en: There's benches for a little walk along the trail.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.4.en: You can see the sea from here.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.5.zh: 从昨晚起一直刮着大风。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.3.example.5.en: The wind has been blowing since last night.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 具有……典型特征；……应有的样子
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.meaning.en: A typical feature; the appearance that should be given

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.connection.zh: 名词＋らしい；名词＋らしさ（名词形式）；名词＋らしく（修饰动词）
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.connection.en: Noun+ らしい ;noun+ らしさ (noun format); noun + らしく (modified verb)

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.note.zh: 表示典型性，给人“很像……、很有……特点”的感觉。本课不是表示传闻或推测的「らしい」。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.note.en: This course is not about anecdotal or speculative "らしい."

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 到处是落叶，总觉得很有秋天的景致吧。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.0.en: There's leaves everywhere. It's always a good fall.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.1.zh: 既然是学生，就要像个学生那样学习。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.1.en: If you're a student, you have to learn like a student.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.2.zh: 这所幼儿园很重视孩子的童真。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.4.example.2.en: The kindergarten values the child as a child.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.connection.zh: い形容词去い／な形容词去だ＋げ；修饰名词用「げな」，修饰动词用「げに」。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.connection.en: Remove final い from an i-adjective or だ from a na-adjective, then add げ. Use げな before a noun and げに before a verb.

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.note.zh: 表示从外表观察到的神情或样子，用法相当于表示样态的「そう」。「～げ」整体按な形容词使用。本课提示不用于长辈或上级。例：楽しげ、悲しげ、寂しげ、恥ずかしげ、得意げ。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.note.en: Describes an outward appearance or expression, similar to appearance-based そう. ～げ behaves as a na-adjective. This lesson advises against using it for elders or superiors. Examples: 楽しげ、悲しげ、寂しげ、恥ずかしげ、得意げ。

chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 他带着得意的神情展示了最新的游戏软件。
chukyu.lesson.5.grammar.5.example.1.en: He showed up-to-date game software with a great look.

chukyu.lesson.5.exerciseInstructions.zh: 第1—3题：過ごす、包まれる、訪れる、浴びる，填入适当形式。第4—7题：気配、住まい、幾分、半ば、息抜き。
chukyu.lesson.5.exerciseInstructions.en: Questions 1–3: use appropriate forms of 過ごす、包まれる、訪れる、浴びる. Questions 4–7: 気配、住まい、幾分、半ば、息抜き。

chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.0.note.zh: 「日を浴びる」表示晒太阳；连接后句用て形。
chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.0.note.en: 日を浴びる means to bask in the sun. Use the te-form to connect to the next clause.

chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.1.note.zh: 「訪れている」表示人们正在到访。
chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.1.note.en: 訪れている describes people visiting at present.

chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.2.note.zh: 被宁静的气氛笼罩，用被动形式「包まれている」。
chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.2.note.en: Use the passive 包まれている to describe being surrounded by a calm atmosphere.

chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.5.note.en: 「9月の半ば」means the middle of September.

chukyu.lesson.5.exercise.6.note.en: 秋の気配 means signs of autumn.

chukyu.question.l5-g1.explanation.zh: ます形「減ります」からますを取って「減りつつある」。
chukyu.question.l5-g1.explanation.en: ます形「減ります」からますを取って「減りつつある」。

chukyu.question.l5-g2.option.0.en: The cause has been fully identified.

chukyu.question.l5-g2.option.2.en: The cause is gradually becoming clear.

chukyu.question.l5-g2.option.3.en: The cause will remain unclear in the future.

chukyu.question.l5-g2.explanation.zh: 「つつある」表示变化正在逐渐进行，并非已经完成。
chukyu.question.l5-g2.explanation.en: つつある indicates that changes are being made gradually and not already completed.

chukyu.question.l5-g3.explanation.zh: 以车站为中心发展，用を中心に。にとって表示评价立场，に代わって表示替代，に加えて表示追加。
chukyu.question.l5-g3.explanation.en: Central to the station, を中心に. にとって indicates an evaluation position, に代わって replaces and に加えて adds.

chukyu.question.l5-g4.explanation.zh: 存在句「店があります」用に标示地点。
chukyu.question.l5-g4.explanation.en: Use に to mark the location in the existence sentence 店があります.

chukyu.question.l5-g5.explanation.zh: 拍照是动作，在动作发生地点后用で。
chukyu.question.l5-g5.explanation.en: Photographing is an action, using で after the action has occurred.

chukyu.question.l5-g6.explanation.zh: 「相談する」是可以由本人决定是否进行的行为。
chukyu.question.l5-g6.explanation.en: "相談する" is an act that can be decided by the person.

chukyu.question.l5-g7.explanation.zh: 「行ける」是可能形式，表示能否去，不是去这一意志行为本身。
chukyu.question.l5-g7.explanation.en: " 行ける " is a Potential form, meaning that it is possible to go, not to the act of will itself.

chukyu.question.l5-g8.explanation.en: らしく modifies the verb 勉強する.

chukyu.question.l5-g9.explanation.zh: 「らしさ」是名词形式，表示孩子应有的特点或童真。
chukyu.question.l5-g9.explanation.en: "らしさ" is a form of noun that represents the child 's desired characteristics or childhood.

chukyu.question.l5-g10.explanation.zh: 「～げ」按な形容词使用，修饰名词「顔」用「得意げな」。
chukyu.question.l5-g10.explanation.en: ～げ behaves like a na-adjective. Use 得意げな to modify 顔.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.meaning.zh: 口语中的缩略形式与连接表达
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.meaning.en: Thumbnail form and connection expression in spoken

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.connection.zh: ではない→じゃない；てしまった→ちゃった；でしまった→じゃった；なければ→なきゃ；ています→てます；ている→てる；ておく→とく；ておいて→といて；のだ→んだ。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.connection.en: ではない→じゃない；てしまった→ちゃった；でしまった→じゃった；なければ→なきゃ；ています→てます；ている→てる；ておく→とく；ておいて→といて；のだ→んだ。

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.note.zh: 教材对照：本ではない→本じゃない；食べてしまった→食べちゃった；飲んでしまった→飲んじゃった；食べなければ→食べなきゃ；食べています→食べてます；食べている→食べてる；食べておく→食べとく；食べておいて→食べといて；食べるのだ→食べるんだ。转折「しかし・だが・が」在口语中常用「だけど・けど・でも」，「ですから」对应「だから」。用于日常口语，注意场合与语气。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.note.en: Textbook comparisons: 本ではない→本じゃない; 食べてしまった→食べちゃった; 飲んでしまった→飲んじゃった; 食べなければ→食べなきゃ; 食べています→食べてます; 食べている→食べてる; 食べておく→食べとく; 食べておいて→食べといて; 食べるのだ→食べるんだ. In conversation, しかし・だが・が often become だけど・けど・でも, and ですから becomes だから. Consider the situation and tone when using these everyday forms.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 不在这一天吃，就没有意义。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.0.example.0.en: There's no point not eating on this day.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.note.zh: 后面接判断或评价，用来说明从某人的立场看某事的意义、难易或重要性等。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.note.en: It is then judged or evaluated to indicate the meaning, difficulty or importance of something from a person ' s position.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 对许多人来说，土用丑日大概就是“忍不住要吃鳗鱼的日子”。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.0.en: For many people, the ugly day of earth is probably a “day that cannot help but eat eel”.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 对留学生来说，日本物价高是个问题。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.1.en: High prices are a problem for students studying abroad.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.2.zh: 对你来说最重要的事情是什么？
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.1.example.2.en: What's the most important thing to you?

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.meaning.en: Can't help it; can't and can't...

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.connection.zh: 动词ない形去ない＋ずに（は）いられない；する→せずにはいられない。也可用「ないではいられない」。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.connection.en: Remove ない from the verb's nai-form and add ずに（は）いられない. Irregular: する→せずにはいられない. ないではいられない is also possible.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.note.zh: 表示感情或欲望难以抑制，无法不做某件事。「は」可以省略。不是单纯的义务或规定。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.note.en: The expression of feelings or desires is hard to contain and cannot do anything. " は " can be omitted. It is not simply an obligation or a regulation.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 到了土用丑日就忍不住要吃鳗鱼。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.2.example.0.en: When the earth is ugly, you can't stop eating eels.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 据说……；根据消息或迹象判断似乎……
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.meaning.en: It is said that ...; it appears from news or indications ...

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词／い形容词普通形＋らしい；な形容词词干／名词＋らしい（现在肯定形不加だ）。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.connection.en: Plain-form verb or i-adjective＋らしい; na-adjective stem or noun＋らしい. Omit だ in the affirmative non-past.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.note.zh: 根据客观信息进行判断或转述消息，带有与所说事情保持一定距离的感觉。与第5课表示典型特征的「Nらしい」区分。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.note.en: Distinguish ～らしい based on evidence or reports from the noun + らしい pattern in Lesson 5, which describes typical qualities.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 据说吃鳗鱼的习惯起源于江户时代的宣传文案。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.example.0.en: The habit of eating eels is said to have originated in the Edo era propaganda case.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.example.1.en: Rumor has it that those two people are getting married.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.example.2.zh: 那个十字路口聚集了很多人。好像是出了事故。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.3.example.2.en: There was a lot of people at that intersection. It was like an accident.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.connection.zh: 普通形＋としたら；名词／な形容词现在肯定形保留だ：本当だとしたら。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.connection.en: Plain form＋としたら. Keep だ in affirmative non-past noun and na-adjective predicates: 本当だとしたら.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.note.zh: 提出假定条件，在此基础上思考结果、选择或应采取的行动。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.note.en: The assumption is made, on the basis of which the results, choices or actions to be taken are considered.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.example.0.en: If it were true, it meant that the effects had lasted for more than 200 years.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.4.example.1.en: If you can re-enter, do you want to be a woman or a man?

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 推论的结果；既定规定；自己决定的习惯
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.meaning.en: Results of inferences; established rules; habits of self-determination

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.connection.zh: V辞书形／Vない形＋（という）ことになる；V辞书形／Vない形＋ことになっている／ことにしている。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.connection.en: Verb dictionary/nai-form + （という）ことになる; verb dictionary/nai-form + ことになっている／ことにしている.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.note.zh: 本课「（という）ことになる」表示由条件或事实推论出的结果。「ことになっている」表示由规则或他人决定的事；「ことにしている」表示自己决定并持续实行的个人习惯。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.note.en: Here （という）ことになる introduces a result inferred from facts or conditions. ことになっている describes a rule or decision made by others; ことにしている describes a personal decision maintained as a habit.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.example.0.zh: 如果是真的，就意味着效果延续了两百多年。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.example.0.en: If it were true, it meant that the effects had lasted for more than 200 years.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.example.1.zh: 如果鳗鱼捕捞量继续这样减少，将来土用丑日恐怕就吃不到鳗鱼了。
chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.example.1.en: If the eels catch continues to decline this way, it is feared that they will not be able to be eaten in the future in an ugly day.

chukyu.lesson.6.grammar.5.example.2.zh: 如果今天之内还没收到他参加聚会的回复，就视为他不参加。

chukyu.lesson.6.exerciseInstructions.zh: 第1—4题：持ち込む、向く、定着する、集中する、跳ね上がる，填入适当形式。第5—8题：主義、効果、生活、防止、宣伝，填入括号中缺少的部分。

chukyu.question.l6-g1.explanation.zh: 「でしまった」缩略为「じゃった」：飲んじゃった。
chukyu.question.l6-g1.explanation.en: The acronym "でしまった" is "じゃった": 飲んじゃった.

chukyu.question.l6-g2.explanation.zh: 「ておいて」缩略为「といて」：買っといて。「買っちゃって」对应買ってしまって；「買ってる」对应買っている；「買わなきゃ」表示必须买，均不表示提前买好备用。
chukyu.question.l6-g2.explanation.en: The acronym "ておいて" is "といて": 買っといて. "買っちゃって" corresponds to 買ってしまって; "買ってる" corresponds to "買っている "; and "買わなきゃ" means that it must be bought, and does not mean that it should be purchased in advance.

chukyu.question.l6-g3.explanation.zh: 「にとって」表示从某人的立场来看，后接评价。
chukyu.question.l6-g3.explanation.en: "にとって" means that someone's position is then evaluated.

chukyu.question.l6-g4.explanation.zh: 「する」接ず的特殊形式是「せず」：心配せずにはいられない。
chukyu.question.l6-g4.explanation.en: する has the special ず-form せず: 心配せずにはいられない.

chukyu.question.l6-g5.explanation.zh: 名词现在肯定形直接接らしい：事故らしい。这里根据迹象判断。
chukyu.question.l6-g5.explanation.en: Attach らしい directly to an affirmative non-past noun: 事故らしい. This expresses a judgment based on signs.

chukyu.question.l6-g6.explanation.zh: 假定“那件事是真的”，用「本当だとしたら」。
chukyu.question.l6-g6.explanation.en: Assume the story is true with 本当だとしたら.

chukyu.question.l6-g7.explanation.zh: 根据条件推论结果，使用「ことになる」。
chukyu.question.l6-g7.explanation.en: Using the "ことになる " , based on conditional extrapolation.

chukyu.question.l6-g8.explanation.zh: 「ことになっている」表示规定或他人决定的事。
chukyu.question.l6-g8.explanation.en: "ことになっている" means something specified or decided by others.

chukyu.question.l6-g9.explanation.zh: 「ことにしている」表示自己决定并持续实行的习惯。
chukyu.question.l6-g9.explanation.en: "ことにしている" describes the habits that you decide on and continue to practice.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.connection.zh: 名词＋だらけ；修饰名词用「NだらけのN」。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.connection.en: Noun＋だらけ; before another noun: NだらけのN.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.note.zh: 表示大量同类事物存在，通常是不理想的状态，如泥、伤、错误等。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.note.en: It means that a great deal of the same kind exists, usually in an undesirable state, such as mud, injury, error, etc.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.0.zh: 满身沙土、伤痕地努力练习。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.0.en: He worked hard to practice with the sand and the scars.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.1.zh: 因为在大雨中走路，鞋子沾满了泥。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.1.en: Because walking in the rain, shoes are covered with mud.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.2.zh: 被上司训斥说“这是一份满是错误的报告”。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.0.example.2.en: “This is a false report” was reprimanded by his superiors.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.meaning.en: Because if you don't, you can't...

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词ない形＋と、动词ない形＋からだ
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.connection.en: verb ない Form+ と , verb ない Form+ からだ

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.note.zh: 「ないと」提出否定条件，「ないからだ」说明理由。常用来解释为什么必须进行某种行为；后半句也可用「命の保証がない」等否定表达。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.note.en: ないと introduces a negative condition; ないからだ explains the reason. The pattern often explains why an action is necessary. The latter clause may use another negative expression such as 命の保証がない.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.0.zh: 这是因为不让身体休息，就无法增重。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.0.en: This is because no physical rest can increase the weight.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.1.zh: 之所以戒掉最喜欢的酒，是因为不戒酒就有生命危险。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.1.en: The reason why I quit my favorite drink is because I'm in danger.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.2.zh: 这里汽车普及率很高。原因是交通不便，没有汽车就无法生活。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.1.example.2.en: There is a high rate of car penetration. The reason for this is that there are no cars without which to live.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋たびに；名词＋のたびに
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.connection.en: verb commentary form + たびに ;noun+ のたびに

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.note.zh: 表示每次发生某事时，总会伴随另一个结果。本课强调不用于日常生活中理所当然的事情，例如“每次早上起床就洗脸”。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.note.en: This lesson emphasizes things that are not taken for granted in everyday life, such as “show your face every morning when you wake up.”

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.example.0.zh: 新入门的弟子们每天早晨到来时，都重复同样的事情。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.example.0.en: Every morning the new entrants come and repeat the same thing.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.example.1.en: I have stomach ache every time I take an exam.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.example.2.zh: 这部电影每看一次都会流泪。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.2.example.2.en: Every time we watch this movie, we cry.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.connection.zh: 名词＋に加え（て）；动词普通形／い形容词＋のに加え（て）；な形容词＋なのに加え（て）。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.connection.en: Noun＋に加え（て）; plain-form verb or i-adjective＋のに加え（て）; na-adjective＋なのに加え（て）.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.note.zh: 在已有的事物或情况上再增加另一项，多用于书面语。教材动词接续列有辞书形、ない形和た形。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.note.en: に加え（て） adds another fact to an existing situation, often in written language. The textbook lists dictionary, ない and た forms for verbs; check the noun and adjective patterns separately.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.0.zh: 除了正餐，体重较轻的新手力士还会被要求睡前吃茶泡饭和香蕉。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.0.en: In addition to regular meals, lightweight freshmen are also required to eat tea and bananas before sleeping.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.1.zh: A先生不仅缺乏工作的积极性，也没有社会常识。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.1.en: Mr. A. not only lacked motivation to work, but also social common sense.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.2.zh: 日本的夏天不仅炎热，而且湿度高，因此不太好过。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.3.example.2.en: Japan ' s summer is not only hot, but it is also very wet, so it is not too good.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.4.meaning.en: At least ...; at the very least...

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.4.note.zh: 这里的「は」提示最低所需的数量或程度，不是单纯提示话题。教材中的饮食和睡眠例句用于理解句型。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.4.note.en: The minimum number or degree of " は" here is not simply the subject. The diet and sleep example in the material is used to understand the sentence.

chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.4.example.0.zh: 新手力士睡前至少吃两碗茶泡饭和十根香蕉。
chukyu.lesson.7.grammar.4.example.0.en: At least two bowls of tea and 10 bananas are to be eaten by the newcomers before they sleep.
